meta.fixture_note: Language-neutral contract for the dashboard expression language. Both the Python evaluator (core/dashboard/expr.py) and the JS evaluator (frontend/lib/expr.js, Phase 3) MUST produce `expect` for each case: parse(expr) then evaluate against `record` with `context`. Numbers compare within 1e-9; null is JSON null. `record` and `context` default to {}. Hand-authored expected values — do NOT regenerate from either evaluator.

outcome_definitions.COMPILED_AGREES: compile_ast() returned; the parameterised SQL executed; and matches(sql_value, python_value) is True under the rule mirrored from tests/test_dashboard_expr.py:20-25 (abs epsilon 1e-9, bools not equal to 0/1).
outcome_definitions.COMPILED_DIVERGES: compile_ast() returned and the SQL executed, but matches() is False — OR the top-level value came back as jsonb 'null' instead of SQL NULL, which breaks compile.py's stated representation contract (compile.py:20-30) even when the decoded values happen to look equal. Cause is named per case.
outcome_definitions.DID_NOT_COMPILE: compile.py raised Uncompilable. No SQL was executed. This is an honest coverage gap and is NEVER counted as a pass.
outcome_definitions.SQL_ERROR: Postgres RAISED while executing the compiled expression. expr is total (expr.py:640 'Never raises for data reasons'), so this is a TOTALITY VIOLATION — the most severe outcome in this spike. NEVER counted as a pass.

known_divergences_from_compile_py.expr_behaviour: Python returns +-inf (expr.py:614-621 has no overflow guard)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: Postgres RAISES 'value out of range: overflow' (verified: select 1e308::float8 * 10::float8)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.note: A real, unguarded totality violation. Arithmetic that overflows a double aborts the query instead of yielding a value.

known_divergences_from_compile_py.construct: xpr.num / xpr.f8 on a JSON number or numeric string beyond DBL_MAX
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: guarded to NULL (a bare cast would RAISE: select '1e999'::float8 -> out of range)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.note: Chosen deliberately: NULL rather than an aborted query. Still a divergence (NULL vs inf) and it is reported here rather than hidden.

known_divergences_from_compile_py.construct: a numeric literal that overflows, e.g. 1e400
known_divergences_from_compile_py.expr_behaviour: parse() builds ('num', inf) (expr.py:193, float() on the token)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: compiler raises Uncompilable; jsonb cannot hold inf (to_jsonb('Infinity'::float8) yields the STRING "Infinity")

known_divergences_from_compile_py.construct: == / != / < <= > >= over JSON numbers with >17 significant digits
known_divergences_from_compile_py.expr_behaviour: Python parses JSON numbers to IEEE doubles first, so 1.0000000000000001 and 1.0000000000000002 are EQUAL
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: jsonb stores `numeric`; the two are DISTINCT. Ordering is routed through xpr.f8 (float8) so `<` matches, but `==` uses jsonb IS NOT DISTINCT FROM and would not.

known_divergences_from_compile_py.construct: lower() / upper() / string ordering on non-ASCII text
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: Postgres lower()/upper() follow the database collation; ordering is pinned to COLLATE "C" here, case mapping is not
xpr.ecma_num reads float8's text output, which is the shortest round-trip only while extra_float_digits >= 0 (PG12+ default 1)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.note: The functions are declared IMMUTABLE despite depending on a GUC. A production deployment would have to pin it.

known_divergences_from_compile_py.construct: today() / now() with no context clock
known_divergences_from_compile_py.expr_behaviour: datetime.now(utc) evaluated once per evaluate() call, i.e. once per record (expr.py:456)
known_divergences_from_compile_py.sql_behaviour: xpr.now_ms falls back to now() == transaction timestamp, i.e. once per query
known_divergences_from_compile_py.note: Every fixture case that uses the clock injects context.now, so this path is NOT exercised by the conformance run.
